channel.title: HeavyMusix: metal news from around the world
channel.description: Metal news written by HeavyMusix: new albums, tours, festivals, the underground and Arizona metal.

item.title: Iron Maiden finally enter the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, and the stars line up to play The Trooper
item.description: It took more than 20 years of eligibility and three nominations, but Iron Maiden are officially in the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. The 2026 ceremony took place Saturday night, November 14, at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, and this year it did not air live. The induction came with a tribute fit for the band: members of Metallica, St. Vincent, Jack Black and more got together to honor Maiden, including a cover of "The Trooper". Musicians from Rage Against The Machine and Motley Crue were part of the salute too. Bruce Dickinson spent years telling anyone who would listen that he did not care about the Hall, but the band's statement thanked the Rock Hall for including former members who were part of the story and said the honor fits their 50th anniversary run with the Run For Your Lives World Tour. Up the Irons!

item.title: Slayer bring Reign In Blood home to Los Angeles; Tom Araya stops the show over crowd safety
item.description: Slayer played their first Los Angeles shows in seven years this weekend, two sold-out nights at the Kia Forum on November 13 and 14 celebrating 40 years of "Reign In Blood", performed front to back. The first night sold out in presales, so a second was added. Support came from Cannibal Corpse, Cavalera playing "Chaos A.D.", and Crowbar. The lineup is Tom Araya on bass and vocals, Kerry King and Gary Holt on guitars and Paul Bostaph on drums. One of the LA nights was halted over safety concerns in the crowd, and video shows Araya scolding fans before the band carried on. Look out for each other in the pit, people.

item.title: Metal Church and Armored Saint roll down the West Coast, with a surprise from Duke Erickson
item.description: Metal Church and Armored Saint kicked off their co-headlining North American run in Bremerton, Washington on November 14, and the night had a special guest: original Metal Church bassist Duke Erickson joined the band on stage. Erickson played on every Metal Church release from the 1982 "Hitman" demo through 1999's "Masterpeace", including the classics "Metal Church" and "The Dark". Next up: Vancouver's Rickshaw Theater tonight (Nov 15), then San Francisco's Great American Music Hall (Nov 17), Roseville (Nov 18) and the Whisky A Go Go in Los Angeles (Nov 19).

item.title: Kittie re-record their darkest album: "Oracle XXV" is out now
item.description: Canada's Kittie have released "Oracle XXV", a re-recorded 25th-anniversary take on songs from 2001's "Oracle". It came out Friday, November 13, almost exactly 25 years after the original dropped on November 12, 2001. "Oracle" was the heavier, darker follow-up to "Spit". It debuted at No. 57 on the Billboard 200 and was the band's only album with bassist Talena Atfield. A new video for "Mouthful Of Poison XXV" is part of the rollout. It follows last year's "Spit XXV" EP and the 2024 comeback album "Fire", which earned Kittie a Juno nomination.

item.title: Tony Iommi and Jorn Lande talk "From The Dark" in a new video interview
item.description: Black Sabbath's Tony Iommi and singer Jorn Lande have shared an official video interview about "From The Dark", Iommi's first solo album in 21 years, released October 23 on BMG. Lande, the Norwegian singer known for Masterplan and Allen-Lande, co-wrote every song and wrote the lyrics. Iommi first worked with him at the 2010 High Voltage festival tribute to Ronnie James Dio. Becky Baldwin plays bass and Karl Brazil plays drums. Iommi had hoped to get Geezer Butler on the record, but Geezer could not do it. The lead single is "World Alone". If you love down-tuned, doom-heavy riffs, this one is worth your time.

item.title: Jinjer's huge 2026: three tours, 50,000 fans in Europe and a stop in Tempe
item.description: Ukraine's Jinjer have had a massive year on the road behind their fifth album "Duél". It started in January with their first European headline tour in six years, opening in Cologne, Germany, and wrapping up in front of more than 50,000 fans across the continent. Next came their first North American headline run since 2024: 37 cities from Ottawa on June 5 to Long Beach on July 25, with Crystal Lake and Entheos as special guests. Arizona got its turn on June 30 at Marquee Theatre in Tempe. Then it was back to Europe in the fall as special guests on Spiritbox's arena tour with Dying Wish, including nights at Manchester's Co-op Live and London's OVO Arena Wembley. Not bad for a band that started out booking its own shows.

item.title: Death Angel's next album is aiming for early 2028
item.description: Bay Area thrash veterans Death Angel are writing and demoing songs for the follow-up to 2019's Grammy-nominated "Humanicide", but singer Mark Osegueda says fans shouldn't expect it before the first quarter of 2028. The plan is to record by summer 2027. The band wants to write a big batch of songs and keep only the best, the same way they built 1990's "Act III". That means the recent singles "Wrath (Bring Fire)", "Cult Of The Used" and "The Never Was" may or may not make the album. Osegueda blamed most of the long gap on the pandemic, which hit drummer Will Carroll hard. Until the album lands, Death Angel keep touring, with shows planned in Europe and Australia plus their yearly holiday gigs.

item.title: Tiamat's Johan Edlund hospitalized; Belgrade show canceled
item.description: Swedish gothic metal pioneers Tiamat canceled their Saturday, November 14 concert at Zappa Barka in Belgrade, Serbia, after founder and singer Johan Edlund suffered a brain hemorrhage. The band shared the news on social media, saying Edlund will stay in the hospital until further notice. They asked fans to keep him in their thoughts. Everyone at HeavyMusix is wishing Johan a full and fast recovery.

item.title: Murderdolls reunite for 25th anniversary shows in 2027
item.description: Wednesday 13 is bringing Murderdolls back. He, Eric Griffin and Acey Slade will play select 2027 shows celebrating 25 years of the debut album "Beyond the Valley of the Murderdolls", with Griffin moving from bass to guitar. Drummer Mike Dupke and bassist Jack Tankersley from Wednesday 13's solo band round out the lineup. The shows honor late members Joey Jordison and Ben Graves, with the blessing of Jordison's family. Wednesday 13 made it clear that nobody is replacing Joey. The three last played together in 2018 at a Ben Graves tribute in Hollywood. Show dates haven't been announced yet.

item.title: Agalloch, Nevermore and Immolation lead Metal & Beer Fest Philly's 10th year
item.description: Decibel's Metal & Beer Fest: Philly turns 10 on Saturday, April 10, 2027 at the Fillmore Philadelphia, and the lineup is stacked: Agalloch headline, with Nevermore, Immolation, Solitude Aeturnus, Undeath, Evoken and Anagnorisis. Solitude Aeturnus will play their second album in full for its 35th anniversary. Tickets are on sale now through Ticketmaster, in two kinds: a music-only ticket, and a 21+ ticket with unlimited craft beer samples, capped at 500. 3 Floyds Brewing presents the beer side, with more than a dozen breweries pouring on the Fillmore's mezzanine.

item.title: North Dakota death metal: Gorgatron's fifth album "Turmoil" lands Dec 11
item.description: Gorgatron, death metal from North Dakota, have shared the title track from their fifth album, "Turmoil". The record comes out December 11 on Time To Kill Records. Proof that heavy music comes from everywhere, even the snowy middle of the map.

item.title: KISS avatar show heading to Las Vegas, likely in 2028
item.description: KISS may be done touring, but they aren't done performing. An avatar-based KISS show is being built for Las Vegas, tentatively for 2028, with the venue still to be announced. It's a project with Pophouse Entertainment, the Swedish company co-founded by ABBA's Björn Ulvaeus, which bought KISS's catalog and name in a deal reported at over $300 million. Expect The Demon, The Starchild, the classics and some new surprises. Paul Stanley says the idea was never to copy a KISS concert. It's meant to be its own experience, built for fans and newcomers alike.

item.title: Phoenix metal this week: DragonForce tonight, Imminence and Trivium coming
item.description: Power metal takes over The Van Buren tonight: DragonForce, with Ensiferum and Rhapsody of Fire, Sunday Nov 15 at 7:30 PM. Coming up: Imminence with Dying Wish at The Van Buren on Nov 27, and Trivium at Arizona Financial Theatre on Dec 2. Heading out? Tag @heavymusixradio in your show pics. And if your band is opening a local bill, send it to submit@heavymusix.com.

item.title: Big week ahead: Trivium, Down, Disfear and Wolf all drop new albums Nov 20
item.description: Friday, November 20 is stacked. Trivium release "Crown In The Grave" on Roadrunner, Down return with "Volume V" on Nuclear Blast, Sweden's Disfear (with At The Gates frontman Tomas Lindberg) unleash "The Last Nail" on Relapse, and Swedish traditional metallers Wolf bring their tenth album, "Hour Of The Wolf." Planning ahead: Powerwolf just announced their "Moral & Madness" 2027 European tour, hitting arenas from Luxembourg to Berlin and Cologne next autumn. Trivium is already in rotation on HeavyMusix Radio. Which of these are you spinning first?

item.title: Band Survival Kit: an animated series for unsigned bands
item.description: Meet Grave Budget: a broke Phoenix metal band learning to run like a business the hard way. Each episode covers one real problem: finding members, splitting money, budgeting, contracts, merch, booking, and not getting ripped off. Each one comes with a free checklist right here on the site. Episode 1, "Wanted: Screamer," is in production.

item.description: Unsigned metal band, anywhere in the world? Send your music, bio, photos and contact info to submit@heavymusix.com. Send a full album or EP, or at least 4 to 5 tracks. Every submission is reviewed, but not every band is selected, and reviews take time. Full details are on the Submit page. It's free, always.
